name: 28587-random1k1k-nemotronh9b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3, one GPU of an a3 node (--gres=gpu:1).
architecture: NemotronHForCausalLM, 8.89B params, hybrid: 27 Mamba2 / 4 self-attention / 25 MLP blocks, hidden 4480, vocabulary 131072, window 131072; FP8 weights by ModelOpt over bf16 activations.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=256, warmup 10%, cooldown 10%, bound.max_requests 1600, safety_seconds 1800.
workload: single-turn plain-text completion, exactly 1024 prompt tokens and 1024 output tokens per request -- min == max on each end, and `ignore_eos` so every generation runs the full length. Greedy, `temperature: 0.0`, `request_format: plain`. Prompts are synthetic and each is distinct, and prefix caching is off. Driven in-process through guidellm's `vllm_python` backend, streaming.
purpose: A bulk text-completion service on a 9-billion-parameter model, serving 256 concurrent users thousand-token prompts and replies on one GPU.
launch:
model: nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2-FP8

# Required, not decorative: the checkpoint's `config.json` carries an `auto_map` pointing at
# `configuration_nemotron_h.py` in the bf16 parent repo, and the config will not load without it.
trust-remote-code: true

tensor-parallel-size: 1
enable-prefix-caching: false
async-scheduling: true
max-num-seqs: 2048
dtype: bfloat16
max-model-len: 4096
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90

# PINNED, AND LOAD-BEARING -- do not drop it as "the default". Built in-process rather than
# through `vllm serve`, this argument falls through to the SchedulerConfig floor of 2048 and every
# 1024-token prefill would be chunked against a four-times smaller budget. 8192 is what a real
# `vllm serve` picks on this device.
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192
